text.p: European Union farm ministers agreed on Wednesday, the third day of marathon talks, a package of mostly unchanged farm prices in 1997/98 (July/June), but put off a proposed cut in aid to wheat farmers, EU officials said.
"It's been agreed," Finnish Farm Minister Kalevi Hemila told Reuters. Only Spain voted against the deal brokered by the Dutch EU Presidency.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler had sought a 1.4 billion Ecu ($1.6 billion) cut in cereals compensation payments, which mainly benefit wealthy grain producers in Britain, France and Germany, to help finance extra aid for beef producers hit by the mad cow disease crisis.
Fischler said he regretted that farm ministers had not agreed the cut at this stage and stressed that the proposal remained on the table.
"Farm spending must remain within the budget," Fischler told a closing news conference, warning that there could be problems in 1998 and that savings must be made in the draft budget.
Dutch Farm Minister Jozias Van Aartsen said that ministers had not wanted to anticipate future reforms and had put forward long "wish lists" of extra demands.
"There are strict budget restrictions in 1998," he warned, adding these should not obstruct the reform negotiations.

The European Commission estimated that grain farmers, who already receive more than 40 percent of EU farm subsidies, were over-paid by 8.5 billion Ecus during the past four years for cuts in support prices agreed under 1992 farm reforms.

But an overwhelming majority of farm ministers disputed this estimate, adding it was unfair to make cereals farmers foot the bill and that there was enough spare cash in the 1997 budget to aid beef producers.

Ministers also called in 1998 for an unchanged five percent rate of cereals set-aside -- a scheme intended to remove costly grain mountains under which farmers must take a certain part of their land out of production to obtain EU subsidies.
"We will make a proposal as quickly as possibly," Fischler told the news conference but declined to give a date.
The Commission does not want to be bounced into a hasty proposal until it has all the necessary crop data.
